release: TOOL 5 NOW ANSWERS THE QUESTION AN OPERATOR IS ACTUALLY ASKING, AND SHIPPED 6.4.1 DID NOT. Two defects went out in 6.4.1 that 423 green offline assertions could not see and that one live run exposed in seconds. FALSE LAUNCH BLOCKER: the recovery sweep finds _dmarc and _domainkey on TXT alone, but the comparison asked the current zone for A/CNAME only, so an empty-vs-empty read scored DROPPED and raised DNS-026 at readiness 1 - a cutover-blocking finding against a DMARC record that had never moved, on every domain that publishes one. PLACEHOLDER IN THE OPERATOR TEXT: recover.js wrapped resolveSoa's bare object in an array before normalising, so the recovered-zone diff read "SOA changed: undefined undefined undefined". resolve.js had already found, documented and fixed that exact trap on the public-resolver path; recover.js carried a second copy of the shape handling and did not. THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE, IS WHAT WAS FIXED: readRecord() in resolve.js is now the only place a node:dns reply becomes a record, and recover.queryZone calls it. AND THE REASON NEITHER WAS CAUGHT: smoke.js had NO coverage of tool 5 at all. It now drives capture, verify and recover through the spawned engine on invariants that hold whatever the internet answers - no finding string may contain a placeholder, nothing may be reported lost with no evidence of what was lost, every finding carries a real rule id, every result names a next action - and SKIPS LOUDLY ("Tool 5 IS NOT CERTIFIED by this run") when the resolvers are unreachable, because a smoke that quietly reports 100% in that state is worse than no check. Replayed over the pre-fix run it catches both defects. PROPAGATION IS REPORTED AS A MEASUREMENT INSTEAD OF A FAULT. The four resolvers were always queried individually, and their disagreement was raised as DNS-003 "resolvers do not agree" at HIGH severity - which is the state a cutover is SUPPOSED to be in while it propagates, so the tool called the zone broken at the exact moment it was working. propagationOf() classifies each resolver against the baseline address and reports how far the repoint has travelled, which resolvers are behind, and the straggler TTL that decides when they catch up; DNS-030 states it, and DNS-003 falls silent for that record ONLY when the split is exactly old-vs-new. A resolver that failed to answer is excluded from the percentage and named, never voted as agreement. THE VERDICT NOW CARRIES AN INSTRUCTION. "BLOCKED - 1 launch-blocking finding" is a status line; an operator mid-cutover needs to know what to do with their hands. verdict.next is written per rule for the findings that can credibly be the worst one, falls back to naming the finding, and appears in the report as a DO THIS NEXT panel, in the CLI as a NEXT line, and in the app status line. It has a branch for every resolver still serving the baseline address, because without it the report congratulated the operator on a cutover that had not started. MAIL HOSTS ARE ASKED FOR MX. The sweep compared addresses only, so mail.<domain> keeping its A record while losing every MX came back "intact" - the failure this module exists for, invisible. Nine mail labels get one extra query rather than all seventy-five, the address and the mail route are carried as separate claims, and DNS-031 (critical, readiness 1) fires when a SURVIVING hostname lost its mail route. A TTL IS REPORTED AS A DEADLINE: the duration in human units plus how long before the repoint it has to be lowered, because afterwards nothing can shorten what is already cached. RULE COUNT 29 -> 31 in the DNS module. The main registry is UNTOUCHED at 161 rules and 1.15.0, suite weight still 0, every rule still severity manual - no score moved. AND ONE DEFECT WAS FOUND ONLY BY LOOKING AT THE RENDER, for the fourth time in this repo: the propagation bar painted the not-yet-moved half in the report's FAILURE RED, so a working cutover read as half-broken at a glance - the precise misreading DNS-030 was written to prevent. Amber now; grey for the resolvers that never answered, because absent evidence gets no colour of its own. Offline suite 423 -> 485 assertions, every addition watched failing first; desktop smoke 7 -> 22; full suite 68/68. STILL UNPROVEN IN THE WILD: a genuine part-propagated split cannot be staged without a real cutover, so that path is unit-tested and rendered, not live-verified. Previous release: DNS & CUTOVER IS TOOL 5. Every check this engine performs began AFTER the domain had already resolved, which left a migration's most expensive failures structurally invisible: a nameserver swap that drops MX and SPF takes a business's email down while every page still scores 100. lib/dns adds three actions matching the three moments of a migration - CAPTURE the zone plus what the current origin serves BEFORE the cutover, which is the only way a later run can tell a DELETED record from one that never existed; VERIFY diffs against that baseline and proves the new origin actually serves with a certificate that covers the name; RECOVER reads the zone the replaced nameservers usually still hold and rebuilds the baseline after the fact, including the subdomains nobody remembers exist. SCORE-NEUTRAL BY CONSTRUCTION - suite weight 0 and every rule severity manual, because a Site Audit routinely runs against a domain the operator does not control and a scored DNS suite would deduct for someone else's nameservers on every run, and would make the score depend on the auditing machine's network path. The registry is UNTOUCHED at 161 rules and 1.15.0; the 29 DNS rules live in their own module and move no score. NEVER THE SYSTEM RESOLVER - four named public resolvers, reported individually, because disagreement between them IS the propagation signal; ENODATA is not ENOTFOUND, and a timed-out resolver is excluded from consensus rather than counted as agreement, so a network hiccup can never render as 'MX unchanged'. FOUR DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY A LIVE RUN AFTER 361 OFFLINE ASSERTIONS WERE ALREADY GREEN: SOA normalised from the wrong shape, www probed with the wrong object so every www reported a FABRICATED outage, a null MX read as real mail routing, and a machine with no IPv6 route reporting the SITE as degraded - a limit of the auditing host presented as a defect of the audited site. FOUR MORE were found only by RENDERING the UI after every DOM assertion passed: stale 'five tools' copy, a bare '0' for the null MX, an Agreement column that rendered empty on a clean run so the reader could not tell 'all agreed' from 'never checked', and DNS-008 firing on every routine re-check because expectCutover existed in the library and had never been exposed. 6.4.1 EXISTS BECAUSE OF THIS FILE: 6.4.0 was published with engine/package.json at 6.4.0 and this metadata still at 6.3.0 - release-gate.js caught it, which is precisely the drift it was written for, and the payload was corrected forward rather than republished under the same number. Previous release: Autonomous pass over the highest-value unfinished work. Four units, none of which crossed the Architecture Freeze. GZIPPED SITEMAPS ARE PARSED. They were recorded present-and-unread because getText decodes UTF-8, which destroys gzip bytes; zlib is a builtin so this cost no dependency. Gzip is detected by MAGIC BYTES, covering a raw .gz file, a Content-Encoding gzip response, and a .gz extension on plain XML. Decompression is capped at 64 MB because a few hundred bytes of gzip can encode gigabytes and an unbounded gunzip in a tool that fetches attacker-controlled URLs is a denial-of-service the AUDITED SITE can aim at the operator. Size accounting uses the UNCOMPRESSED length, or a 2 MB gzip carrying 80 MB of XML would pass a limit it plainly breaks. THE TWO NUMBERS EXPLAIN THEMSELVES. A run read 'score 50, quality 84, PASSED WITH WARNINGS' with no statement of what any of them measures and two apparently contradicting. Both are now labelled and carry the reason they differ: one is the share of GRADED checks that passed, weighting every check equally; the other is registry-weighted over rules that provably ran, so one critical failure costs more than ten minor ones. Presentation only - the scoring model is frozen and nothing recomputes it. TEST-SUITE ENVIRONMENT SWEEP, after the PID-modulo port. ui-script.test.js derived its port from hrtime and then CONNECTED to it, the same silent talk-to-a-stranger class; it now asks the OS for a free port AND aborts if the spawned child died, so asserting against another process is impossible rather than unlikely. Two fixture suites moved off fixed ports. AND THE REAL FIND: three suites pin assertions to stored live runs that HAVE BEEN DELETED, so roughly fourteen assertions in readiness plus the anti-fixture cross-check in score-evaluation have been silently dead while the run reported 66/66. Not fixable by inventing baselines - re-pinning to a current run means deriving expectations from today's behaviour, the exact trap those suites exist to prevent. The skip is now LOUD and NAMES the missing artifacts. CERTIFICATION.md MATCHES THE PRODUCT AGAIN. The record that answers 'can this ship' claimed engine 2.4.0, registry 1.13.0, 142 rules, package 4.5.0 and 58 suites while the product was 4.1.0, 1.15.0, 161, 6.2.0 and 66 - drifted through two majors with nothing to catch it. Reconciled, and now GUARDED by verifyCertification() in the version-authority suite, with a negative control that proves the verifier reports dirty on a deliberately stale copy.
